correctness.rationale: The finite-interval distance formula follows from a signed-jump lower bound plus explicit paths for both optimal jump counts, including the small-gap boundary case. The five-row residue difference table is injective for every k>=3 and separates all vertex pairs with landmarks 0,1,2k+1. The only possible resolving pair consists of endpoints; at n=b+2 a specific collision appears, and at n>=b+3 a six-versus-five distance count excludes it. Independently generated BFS tests verified 21,945 ordered source–target distances across 13 graphs, as well as the stable residue expressions for k=3,...,300. Finite checks are not substituted for the full proof.

originality.rationale: The 2022 primary source explicitly conjectures the odd-parameter case and proves the corresponding even-jump result. Earlier 2019 metric-dimension work establishes only jumps <=6 for three generators; 2022 and 2024 Toeplitz partition-dimension articles do not imply a 3-landmark metric basis for odd b>=13. Targeted semantic mathematical-record and published-literature searches identified no equivalent result. The original lower-bound device and explicit uniform basis are distinguished from the previously conjectured scalar equality. Publication priority remains subject to unindexed literature.

value.rationale: The finding settles one full parity subfamily of a precisely stated infinite-parameter 2022 conjecture with a basis independent of graph order. Its boundary-independent exact Toeplitz metric and injective residue signature explain the mechanism and give reproducible ways to design metric landmarks. The k>=3 family is not an arbitrary numerical slice: b≡1 mod4 is the congruence class where one fixed three-landmark choice resolves every interval.
